question: Does CvSU’s ASEANO newsletter explicitly connect its Imus watershed project listing to PEMSEA’s published watershed-mapping report?

sourceReviews.finding: CvSU’s January 2021 newsletter gives the parent project title “Biophysical Characterization, Vulnerability, and Pollution Assessment in Imus River Watershed” and states that CvSU will work on Study 4: “Mapping and Characterization of Imus River Watershed Using GIS and RS.” This explicitly connects the project listing to the mapping study as one ASEANO component.

The Research Center listing uses a near-identical parent project title and names Noel A. Sedigo, PEMSEA funding and November 2020-April 2021. The January newsletter gives January-June 2021; the differing periods remain unresolved.

PEMSEA’s publicly available report title matches the CvSU newsletter’s Study 4 mapping title, and the report identifies CvSU authors including N.A. Sedigo. This confirms the report as a Study 4 mapping output; neither source establishes it as the complete parent-project deliverable.

confirmedLink.parentProject: Biophysical Characterization, Vulnerability, and Pollution Assessment in Imus River Watershed (ASEANO)
confirmedLink.component: Study 4: Mapping and Characterization of Imus River Watershed Using GIS and RS
confirmedLink.publicReport: ASEANO 2020-2021, Subproject 1: Mapping and Characterization of Imus River Watershed Using Geographic Information System and Remote Sensing Technology
confirmedLink.evidence: The CvSU newsletter explicitly assigns the mapping study to CvSU; the official PEMSEA report has the matching mapping title and CvSU authorship.
confirmedLink.boundary: This confirms one mapping component, not every expected parent-project output or a fish-specific study.

reportReview.interpretation: The report remains watershed and hydrology context only. It provides no reviewed fish survey, taxon list or occurrence table; printed watershed maps are not reusable fishing geometry.

nextAction: Continue looking for the remaining ASEANO reports, full CvSU parent-project outputs and the separate Bacoor fish-tissue study. Do not treat the watershed map as fish evidence or reusable fishing geometry.
